message.content:
There are 7 distinct beads and 7 distinct positions in the hexagon, so without considering symmetries there are

\[
7! = 5040
\]

arrangements.

The symmetry group of the hexagonal arrangement is the dihedral group \(D_6\), which has

\[
12
\]

symmetries: 6 rotations and 6 reflections. Since all beads have distinct colors, no non-identity symmetry can leave an arrangement unchanged: any nontrivial symmetry moves at least one bead to a different position, which would require two beads to have the same color.

Therefore, every equivalence class has exactly 12 arrangements, so the number of distinct arrangements is

\[
\frac{7!}{12}=\frac{5040}{12}=420.
\]

The answer is 420.
